additional_info.subject: RE: R: ID0449204-DC/Si-D/IT-[multiple] DC connector exploded CRM:02678000377
additional_info.body:
Dear RC-IT Team,
I am reaching out via ticketing system in regards of the incident happened in Rome with the DC plugs melted in the bus. A Taskforce chat has been already in place in the last hours, and preliminary analysis and results have been already shared by Product Care. I am writing you on behalf of Sicharge D Product Care Team, who follows in copy, in order to channel the technical communication and analysis in the ticket.
Incident Summary:
On the evening of September 10, 2025, several SiCharge D charging units reported failures related to their CCS plugs. The affected units and their approximate failure times are as follows:
Charger Name 35
(Serial Number: 170004371) - Failure Range: 08:00 – 08:30 PM
Charger Name 25
(Serial Number: 170004326) - Failure Range: 09:30 – 10:00 PM
Charger Name 18
(Serial Number: 170004376) - Failure Range: 10:30 – 11:30 PM
Current Status and Preliminary Analysis:
Our Product Care team is actively engaged and supporting the ongoing investigation. The preliminary analysis results are available in the attachment to this email for your review, and were previously shared via MS Teams.
It has been confirmed that the affected chargers were in active use during the months of May, June, July, and August, indicating established operational history.
Two out of the three reported cases logged the same EVMAC in their fault events. While this can occur with certain EVs, it currently impedes the support team's ability to definitively verify if the same bus was involved in multiple fault occurrences.
Observations and Context:
We note the confirmed heavy rainfall in Rome on the morning of September 10, 2025, which may be a contributing environmental factor.
Side scratches have been observed on the reported CCS plugs. This is a common symptom indicative of plugs that may have been left on the ground or handled improperly.
Action Items for RC-IT:
To facilitate a comprehensive investigation and ensure rapid restoration of service, please prioritize the following actions:
Information on Fourth Charger:
Provide details regarding the fourth charger that was reportedly affected. Please provide information on the serial number, time of failure, EV serial number, and photos’ folder as per the other chargers.
Immediate Repair, Spares and Faulted Cables Collection:
Promptly order replacement CCS cables for all affected units.
Execute repairs as soon as the spare parts are available.
Collect the affected cables and ship them as soon as possible to Product Care for further investigation. Please let us know once you have the damaged cables in your possession, so that we can instruct you where and to whom to ship them.
EcoG logs Collection:
For completion of analysis, we would need to collect the EcoG logs from the affected chargers and the affected charging sessions.
It would be necessary to organize a session where the affected chargers are powered on, to enable remote collection of EcoG logs by ES Team..
Environmental Assessment:
Request surveillance footage from the depot operator for September 10, 2025. This footage is crucial to assess the amount of rainfall and identify any potential water accumulation in the depot area.
Operational Handling Assessment:
Request surveillance footage from the depot operator focusing on the handling of CCS plugs by drivers and bus operators. We need to verify correct plug insertion prior to charging and proper placement back into the charger plug holder at the end of each charging session. This is particularly relevant given the observed side scratches.
Request surveillance footage from the depot operator focusing on the affected charging sessions which brought to melting of cables. We need to verify if any eventual mishandling of the CCS plugs during the charging processes while the failures happened.
On-site Charger Inspection:
Arrange for a visit to the depot (or delegate to the bus operator) to physically check the affected chargers for any signs of water ingress.
Detailed Photo Documentation:
Provide high-quality photographs of the charging inlet on each affected bus. This visual evidence is vital for our
analysis
.
Commissioning Reports:
Provide the commissioning report for each of the impacted charging units. Please provide this documentation both in this ticket and ensure it is uploaded to the asset page of each charging unit in ISP.
Channeling of Official Communication:
Please refer to this ticket
ID0449204
as the only official channel for technical communication and documentation exchange. Kindly avoid using parallel communication channels between all stakeholders involved (CS ES, RC-IT, Product Care).
Your prompt attention to these items is highly appreciated. We are here to provide any further support required from the Product Care and Engineering teams.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
Smart Infrastructure

Expert Services

13629 Berlin, Germany

additional_info.subject: Status of repair
additional_info.body: RC-IT confirmed that repair of the affected chargers has been completed on 30.09.2025

additional_info.subject: Status Update
additional_info.body:
Damaged cables have reached the logistic supplier facilities in LPZ.
Open points from Product Care (To be verified with the RC). PrCare has been required to get in touch with RC directly:
-
Did you check the other plugs for signatures of Driving over/mechanical damages etc.?
- many of the contacts are bent, mostly the auxiliary ones. Is there any explanation e.g. by the employees trying to separate them by force from the bus?
- why is there a feather in one of the plugs?
Further observations from PrCare:
similar appearance of all 4 samples
same failure mechanism -> intrusion of water -> flashover
all plugs feature bent contacts
prior damage due to driving over seems unlikely, since not all feature strong scratches on the sides and one plug (no4) only shows minimal housing gap at the bottom.

additional_info.subject: Status update
additional_info.body:
Repairs have been performed.
This topic is currently being maintained by PrCare and no pending actions in the tickets are remaining. This ticket will be closed.
